questions.q: What is Confluent Cloud, per this lesson?
options: A fully managed Kafka-as-a-service, run by the company founded by Kafka's original creators, giving you real Kafka without operating a broker yourself
A completely different messaging system unrelated to Kafka
A free, open-source tool with no company behind it
A Kafka Streams application you deploy locally
questions.explain: It's still real, open-source Kafka underneath — just fully managed by Confluent.

questions.q: What does creating a cluster in Confluent Cloud replace from the self-hosted world?
options: Manually provisioning VMs, installing Kafka, and choosing broker count and replication factor by hand
Nothing — clusters do not exist in Confluent Cloud
The concept of a topic entirely
The Kafka wire protocol itself
questions.explain: You pick a cluster type and region from a console instead of doing that provisioning yourself, as shown in the cluster-creation screenshot.

questions.q: In the topic-creation screenshot for the 'users' topic, what setting is still required, exactly as in self-hosted Kafka?
options: A partition count
A ZooKeeper connection string
A physical server hostname
A broker's disk size in gigabytes
questions.explain: Managed doesn't remove the concept of a partition count — it just removes the need to provision the machine holding those partitions.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what stays exactly the same whether a client connects to a self-hosted Kafka cluster or Confluent Cloud?
options: The Kafka producer/consumer wire protocol and concepts like topics, partitions, and consumer groups
The billing model
The need to patch broker software manually
The physical location of the servers
questions.explain: A client application uses the same Kafka client APIs regardless of whether the cluster is self-hosted or managed.

questions.q: What genuinely disappears when moving to Confluent Cloud, per the lesson's comparison?
options: Broker VMs, a self-run ZooKeeper/KRaft cluster, and hardware-level capacity planning
The concept of a topic
The ability to have more than one partition
The Kafka producer and consumer APIs
questions.explain: Billing shifts to throughput and storage instead of server count, and there's no coordination layer left for you to run.
